beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable at runtime (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never hard-code or commit it; provide a .env.example placeholder file instead.

Store and rotate long‑lived secrets (connection strings, DB keys, OPENAI_API_KEY) in a secure secret store (Azure Key Vault) and grant the application least‑privilege access (managed identity) rather than embedding secrets in code or config files.

Enable TLS (SSL) with certificate verification on the MongoDB client connection; use the SRV/standard connection string options that enforce TLS and turn off tlsAllowInvalidCertificates in production.

Configure the MongoDB/PyMongo connection pool (maxPoolSize, minPoolSize) and sensible serverSelectionTimeoutMS/heartbeatFrequencyMS to avoid frequent reconnects and to control concurrent connections for the managed cluster.
Use retryable reads/writes with exponential backoff for transient network or throttling errors; implement idempotent upserts for seeding to avoid duplicate data when retries occur.

Provision throughput thoughtfully: use autoscale or database/collection-level throughput to match workload, and avoid running large analytics against a shared, low-throughput OLTP provisioned database without throttling or dedicated capacity.

Create indexes that support the detector's most common patterns: indexes on transaction_id, from_account, to_account, timestamp (often compound, e.g., {from_account:1, timestamp:-1} and {to_account:1, timestamp:-1}) to make chain-following and time-window queries efficient.

When using graph traversal ($graphLookup), limit recursion with maxDepth and restrict starting conditions so the server work is bounded; if server-side graph ops are unsupported or expensive, implement client-side bounded BFS/DFS with batched queries and cycle detection.
Avoid returning or processing entire documents when not needed: use projection ($project) to include only fields needed for AML rules and narrative generation to reduce network and memory pressure.

Use server-side aggregation where possible to filter and pre-aggregate (place $match early, $project to narrow fields, $limit early) but set allowDiskUse and set reasonable maxTimeMS to protect against long‑running pipelines.

When storing vector embeddings for similarity search, keep a consistent embedding dimension, normalize vectors if using cosine similarity, and store them in a dedicated field with a matching vector index configured (choose HNSW/IVF/DiskANN parameters appropriate to recall/latency needs).

Tune vector index parameters (e.g., efConstruction, efSearch, nprobe or equivalent) according to dataset size and latency/retrieval quality needs, and validate recall with a held-out test set rather than default settings.

Avoid unbounded in-memory graph expansion during chain traversal: fetch neighbors in batches (use cursor batch_size), persist intermediate checkpoints so long traversals can be resumed and avoid timeouts/OOM.

Design transaction documents for efficient queries: include explicit from_account, to_account, timestamp, amount, currency, and normalized reference fields (e.g., reference_id) and ensure fields used in filters/joins are indexed and typed consistently.

Protect PII: enable encryption at rest (platform default), and consider client-side field-level encryption for extremely sensitive fields (account numbers, SSNs) so data remains encrypted in the DB and logs.
Use firewall rules and private endpoints (VNet) to restrict cluster access to known hosts or application subnets rather than opening the DB to the public internet.

Instrument and monitor query performance and resource metrics (RU/s consumption, operation latency, index usage, slow queries) and configure alerts to catch spikes caused by heavy aggregations or full-collection scans.

Seed test/sample data idempotently using upsert with a unique key (e.g., synthetic transaction_id) and make tests deterministic; never modify other databases—limit scripts to the sample_banking_01 database.

Limit aggregation memory and server impact by filtering early, avoiding $lookup/$graphLookup on unindexed fields, and prefer keyed joins on indexed reference fields or precomputed denormalized data for heavy analytic workloads.

Implement observability and resumability for the detector: log which chains were processed, store processed checkpoints and flagged-chain artifacts in a durable collection with unique IDs to allow retries and auditability.
